rationale: Masking personal identities in displayed data protects privacy from disclosure.
Requires an encrypted channel for exchanging patient data, with no mention of alteration detection.
Requires a verification that reports records altered since being saved, i.e. alteration detection.
Anti-malware scanning and quarantine of malicious files is detecting and blocking malware.
Idle session termination and lock explicitly aims to limit exploitation of an unattended session (rule 7).
Per-clinic encryption keys keep each clinic's records undecryptable by others, protecting against disclosure.
Restricts who may create, modify or cancel bookings, which is a write-access restriction (rule 3).
Limits applications to authorised screen regions and hides other content, restricting access to information.
Account recovery only after the user proves control of the registered email is identity verification.
Grants write and delete permissions only to explicitly privileged accounts, restricting who can modify data.
Verifying the ownership mark of firmware and rejecting modified marks detects alteration and checks the origin of the image.
Ensures all hubs and apps authenticate the user only with the current credential, which is credential-based authentication.
Validates configuration values for type and range and aborts on failure, a data validity check.
Only physicians may amend diagnoses and other roles are rejected, restricting who can modify data.
Limits each app to the readings it needs and conceals others, restricting read access.
Detects manipulation of the signed booking data and cancels the reservation, protecting data from tampering.
Enforces credential reset across modules so identity checks use the latest credential.
Restricts edits of salary and bank records to authorised roles, a modification restriction.
A cryptographic digest is computed so later changes to the file can be detected.
Requires valid developer credentials before accepting a build request, which is authentication.
Validates signatures and blocks items altered without authorisation, detecting alteration; origin verification is not stated.
Rejects values not conforming to the declared type and keeps the stored row unmodified, preserving data validity.
Separate encryption key hierarchies keep each customer's data unreadable to others.
Encrypted transport prevents eavesdroppers from reading page content.
Requires detection of tampered sales data so the accuracy of the data can be trusted.
Sets minimum strength for the PIN or passphrase used to authenticate the cardholder.
Prevents other processes from modifying or deleting saved recordings, protecting data from unauthorised change.
Rejecting messages with duplicated nonces or counters blocks replay attacks.
Restricts write access to sales figures to authorised analysts so others cannot change them.
Requires detecting any alteration of the scenario file between release and loading.
Requires an identifier, a pairing credential and confirmation of identity before enrolment.
Limits viewing of personal or business-critical fields to permitted roles.
A MAC verified before display or processing detects alteration of reservation records; origin verification is not stated.
A tamper-evident mark allows any modification of the statement to be detected.
Returns only data the requesting account is permitted to read, restricting read access.
The integrity mark must remain detectable despite deliberate editing aimed at erasing it, covering tamper detection and resisting intentional attack.
Erasing buffers with payment details prevents later sessions from reading residual data, protecting against disclosure.
Only a signed-in administrator may modify policy settings, restricting who can modify configuration.
Requires a registered account name and matching credential before accepting device commands, which is authentication.
